To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the constrained l 2 -based Volterra system modelling algorithm can be used to obtain models of a system with a finite memory, and that the resulting models can be used to predict its future behaviour.

the Volterra series-based models obtained with the l q -constricted least squares method for q = 2, 1. 5, 1 are better than the models obtained using the standard l 2 -constrained least square method.
the Volterra series-based models obtained for q ≥ 1 can be used for the characterization of the non-linearity and for the prediction of the system’s output.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of a simple non-linear system model based on constrained least squares estimation.
the development of a Volterra series-based nonlinear system modelling algorithm that is able to provide a trade-off between accuracy and model complexity.
the development of a simple, yet efficient, algorithm that can be applied to systems with unknown structure and a priori information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for q > 2, the models obtained are too sparse to be of any practical use, for 2 ≥ q ≥ 1.5, the models obtained have a better fit to the system’s input-output behaviour, and for q = 2 they are more accurate in terms of the model’s ability to capture the nature of the non-linearity.
the proposed method is a very useful tool for system identification, but that it should be used carefully and with the knowledge of its limitations.
for a given system, there is a trade-off between the model’s complexity and accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model obtained for q =2, with its sparse solution, is the most appropriate model for a system with limited a prior knowledge.
the proposed algorithm can be successfully employed to estimate the Volterra series-based models for systems with a finite memory and bounded input-output maps, using short data records.
the algorithm presented here is a simple, robust and efficient way to estimate Volterra series models, even for systems with unknown memory length.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to obtain an adequate model of a system, it is important to take into account the nature of the data available and the desired properties of the model.
a constrained least squares algorithm with 1 ≤ q ≤ 2 is capable of providing good approximations of a non-linear system’s behaviour with a limited a priori information and short data records.
the proposed algorithm is able to provide a model of the system with a guaranteed accuracy for a wide range of values of D, even if the number of samples is very small.
